# projects

Projects group the instances, disks, and networks that belong together.

## GET /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/activity

Operation `tenant_activity_list`.

A tenant's change feed: the audit events that concern it, oldest first, optionally narrowed to one project. Tenant-member gated; another tenant's feed is a 404.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `after_seq` | query | no | integer (uint64) | Return events with `seq > after_seq`. Default 0. |
| `limit` | query | no | integer (uint32) | Maximum events to return, newest last. Default and cap follow `DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` and `MAX_PAGE_SIZE`. |
| `project` | query | no | string (uuid) | Only events that concern this project. |

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [TenantActivity](schemas.md#tenantactivity)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/projects/{project_id}

Operation `project_delete`.

Delete a project. Returns 404 when the project does not exist or belongs to a different tenant.

The store enforces a dependency gate: a project that still owns instances, VPCs, floating IPs, or project-scoped images is refused with `409 Conflict` naming what remains. Nothing cascades. A project is the ownership root for everything a tenant provisions and none of it back-references the project, so deleting an occupied one would leave instances running and billing, floating IPs holding their addresses, and all of it unreachable through the project-scoped listings that are the only way a tenant enumerates them.

| Parameter | In | Required | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `project_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |
| `tenant_id` | path | yes | string (uuid) |  |

Responses:

- `204`: successful deletion
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
